newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq closes higher, helped by soaring long bond.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq closes higher, helped by soaring long bond.

text.p: The Nasdaq market closed higher on Wednesday as ready cash poured into technology issues, enticed by the soaring 30-year Treasury bond.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 15.73 points, or one percent, to close unofficially at 1588.05. Advancing issues beat declines six to five on total volume of 733 million shares.
"There were bids and buyers all over the place," one trader said.
Said another trader: "Technology continued to be very strong pretty much across the board."
"There seems to be a lot of cash on the side and it poured into the market. The bond market was strong most of the day, which helped," he added.
The 30-year bond rose 30/32 from Tuesday, with its yield falling to 6.32 percent from 6.38 percent -- its lowest since February 16, 1996.
Ascend Communications Inc rose 5/16 to 53-7/16 after the company said PSINet Inc agreed to a "major deployment" of MAX TNT wide-area network (WAN) switches.
Ascend's gain came atop a 6-3/8 point gain seen Tuesday, when it was also the most heavily traded Nasdaq issue.
Shares of 3Com Corp fell 2-1/4 to 55-3/4 after the company told analysts it restated its fiscal 1997 earnings and its current margins were at the lower end of a targeted range.
